text: Lesson 8 covered embedding versus referencing as a MongoDB decision. Cosmos DB's Core API faces the exact same fundamental choice, but with one genuinely new factor layered on top: Request Units turn every read and write into a metered cost.

An order and its line items, read together on every request, are a strong embedding candidate — one document, one read. A product catalog referenced by thousands of orders is a poor embedding candidate, since embedding it everywhere duplicates it and breaks updates. That reasoning is identical to MongoDB's — what's new is that every option here now has a metered RU cost, not just a query-complexity cost.

Because a container has one partition key, a useful pattern is embedding data so everything typically read together lands in the same logical partition, avoiding cross-partition queries — real and possible, but more expensive in RU terms. Then validate the modeling choice against actual RU cost under real traffic, not just query convenience.

A modeling decision that looks reasonable for query convenience can be the wrong choice once its RU cost under real traffic is accounted for. Next up: Request Units and throughput provisioning — what an RU actually is, and how to size it correctly.
